reviews.name: Kerry G
reviews.text: I can’t recommend CJG Earthworks & Pools highly enough. Craig and his team of quiet achievers, Mick and Joel, stepped in to rescue us after we’d been left in the lurch with a drainage job.

faq.q: How long does a pool take to build?
faq.a: It depends on the pool and the site. Most fibreglass projects are done in about four to six weeks. A custom concrete pool usually takes around three to four months from signing to swimming. Both include design, approvals, site works and the finishing touches.

faq.q: When is the best time to start?
faq.a: Autumn or winter. Spring is the busiest time for pool builders and lead times stretch out. Building through the cooler months means the pool is finished and filled before Canberra's swimming season starts.

faq.q: Do you build concrete or fibreglass?
faq.a: Both. Fibreglass is quicker to install and needs less cleaning. Concrete can be any size and shape and fits more naturally into a landscape. The site, soil and budget usually decide it — the free consultation is the time to talk it through.

faq.q: Do you handle the ACT approval?
faq.a: Yes. In the ACT a new pool needs building approval and a compliant pool barrier before it can be used. They handle the approval process and make sure the pool and fencing meet the current safety rules.

No. Site cuts for houses, sheds and estates, excavation, drains, concrete and paving are just as in demand. They'll also fill in a pool you no longer use and pave over it, or respray and repave a tired concrete pool.

faq.q: Do you do the landscaping and decking too?
faq.a: Yes. Decking, landscaping, water features and general backyard renovation can go on the same quote as the pool.

notOnThePage: No builder or pool licence number is published anywhere on their site, so no licence is claimed and the word 'licensed' is not used.
No insurance, warranty or guarantee wording is published, so none is claimed.
No number of years is published (only 'many years of experience'), so no years figure is used. ABN Lookup shows the company since Dec 2014, but that is not on their site.
Craig's surname and formal role aren't published, so neither is used. Mick and Joel appear only in the review.
No prices are published. The 2020 blog's '20-30% cheaper' fibreglass figure is general industry talk, not their pricing, so it is left out.
The 11 'pool design' images on their homepage (2016 uploads) look like manufacturer range photos, not CJG jobs, so they are not used. Nor are their Shutterstock blog images or old theme headers.
The one Google review is shown only in its best_for_demo form, marked shortened. No other reviews exist to use.
